simple.meaning: עָצַל (ʻâtsal) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to lean idly , i.e. to be indolent or slack.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Judges, beginning at Judges 18:9. The surrounding contexts include land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עָצַל (H6101) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: עָצַל (ʻâtsal) / H6101 is traced through Judges 18:9 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.short: to lean idly , i.e. to be indolent or slack
definitions.full: H6101. atsel [ עָצֵל ] verb Niph`al be sluggish (Late Hebrew in derived species, and derivatives; compare Arabic III. stick fast in coitu , Lane 2086 ; Syriac be stupid ); — Imperfect 2masculine plural לָלֶכֶת אַלתֵּֿעָֽצְלוּ Judg 18:9 be not sluggish in going .

occurrences.englishText: They said, “Arise, and let’s go up against them; for we have seen the land, and behold, it is very good. Do you stand still? Don’t be slothful to go and to enter in to possess the land.
